checked.replacement: In February 2025 the NDPC fined Meta USD 32.8 million for behavioural advertising without consent and unlawful cross-border transfers. Meta challenged it in the Federal High Court, Abuja, and on 3 November 2025 Justice James Omotosho entered the parties' settlement as a consent judgment. According to the leaked agreement, the NDPC's final orders, including the fine, were set aside in exchange for general compliance commitments and payment of the NDPC's legal fees.

notes: Most serious: cases[2] (and appeal.court, quirks[2]) describe the Meta NDPC case as an unfinished settlement; it ended with a consent judgment on 3 November 2025 that set the USD 32.8m fine aside. Payment or further appeal of the FCCPC USD 220m fine was not established; a TechCabal headline of 1 October 2026 says Meta is appealing a ruling on ad tracking (page refused WebFetch, 403), so cases[0]'s 'not confirmed' wording should stay. Nairametrics wrongly says no orders were set aside; the FCCPC's own release (Order 7 set aside) is preferred. NDPA statute text could not be fetched, so section numbers remain secondary.
